value.text:
Hamburg University of Technology (Technische Universität Hamburg, TUHH) is a public technical university in the Harburg district of Hamburg, Germany. It was established on 22 May 1978 as Technische Universität Hamburg-Harburg. In 2018 the institution changed its name to Technische Universität Hamburg while continuing to use the TUHH abbreviation. The university's buildings are concentrated around a campus between Eißendorfer Straße and Am Schwarzenberg-Campus, with additional facilities elsewhere in the city. Its Wikidata institution-level coordinate is 53.4609583° N, 9.9695056° E, whereas the English Wikipedia infobox gives 53.4564972° N, 9.9683306° E beside its institutional address. The two coordinates are not identical and neither is established by this evidence as a precise campus or headquarters point.

Research activities began in 1980, and teaching followed in 1982/83. The university organizes teaching through study divisions and research through interdisciplinary departments and fields rather than traditional faculties. The programmes described include civil and environmental engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, mathematics, mechanical engineering, chemical and process engineering, and management-oriented technology studies.

The research portfolio includes advanced materials and bioprocesses, aviation and maritime technology, cyber-physical and medical systems, environmental and energy systems, and logistics, mobility and infrastructure. The German Wikipedia profile reports approximately 7,400 students in 2023, while a separate Wikidata observation gives 7,223 for that year; those source measurements should remain distinct. The university also reports personnel and financial figures of varying scope and reference periods, including a EUR 153.5 million annual budget for 2021. Andreas Timm-Giel is identified as president.
